description: A .NET 10 extension-based CLI framework (the `az` binary) for Azure resource management, with an out-of-process AI agent fallback (GitHub Copilot SDK), an interactive Terminal UI, and mirrored PowerShell cmdlets. Project codename is Azclips; user-scoped state lives under ~/.azclips.

generatedAgainst.note: README.md, AGENTS.md and eng-docs/spec/ARCHITECTURE.md contain stale claims (.NET 9, in-process AgentEngine/Azure OpenAI, Bootstrapper class). This catalogue reflects the ACTUAL code.

modules.title: Getting Started
modules.summary: Orientation for new users and contributors: what Azclips is, how it is built, how to run the `az` CLI and the PowerShell modules.

children.title: Overview & Architecture
children.prompt: Explain what Project Azclips is and give the 10,000-foot architecture. It is a .NET 10 (net10.0) extension-based CLI producing the `az` binary, with an out-of-process AI agent fallback and mirrored PowerShell cmdlets. Cover the four client surfaces (CLI, PowerShell, interactive TUI, agent-mode) all sharing one DI composition root. Trace the happy path: `src/CLI/Program.cs:31` Main -> `AzclipsServiceProvider.Initialize` (`src/Core/Core.DependencyInjection/AzclipsServiceProvider.cs:67`) -> `ExtensionDispatcher.Parse` (`src/CLI/Parser/ExtensionDispatcher.cs:44`) -> `IEngine.OpenExecutionSession` (`src/Core/Core.Abstractions/IEngine.cs:8`, `src/Core/Core.Engine/Engine.cs:39`) -> `ExecutionSession.RunAsync` (`src/Core/Core.Engine/ExecutionSession.cs:57`). Then explain the failure path: on exception `Program.TryAgentFallbackAsync` (`src/CLI/Program.cs:281`) spawns the TUI in `--agent-mode` (`src/CLI/Program.cs:320`). IMPORTANT: correct the record vs stale docs — target is net10.0 NOT .NET 9 (`global.json:3`, `src/Directory.Build.props:5`); the composition root is `AzclipsServiceProvider`, there is no `Bootstrapper` class; the agent uses the GitHub Copilot SDK, not Azure OpenAI. Note the Azclips product naming (product `Shared.props:3`, config dir `~/.azclips` `src/Core/Core.Abstractions/HomePaths.cs:14`). Include a system-context Mermaid diagram (dark-mode colors).

children.title: Environment Setup
children.prompt: Step-by-step environment setup. Prerequisites: .NET 10 SDK pinned to 10.0.203 (`global.json:3`, roll-forward latestMinor), PowerShell 7+, an Azure subscription for live calls, and PlatyPS 1.0.1 only for help artifact generation (see `README.md:73`). Explain the solution layout from `azclips.slnx` (src/CLI, 10 Core projects, 6 Extensions, TUI, Agent, src/PS, tests, tools/Help). Show build commands: `dotnet build -c Release azclips.slnx` produces `artifacts/Release/Core.Cli/az`; note `scripts/deploy.sh` and the `build/` PowerShell scripts. Explain the artifacts output convention from `Shared.props:8` (OutputPath = artifacts/$(Configuration)/$(ExtName)/) and the shared build properties in `src/Directory.Build.props` (Nullable, ImplicitUsings, TreatWarningsAsErrors). Show where user state lands: `~/.azclips` (`src/Core/Core.Abstractions/HomePaths.cs:14`) and `{LocalApplicationData}/.azclips` for profiles/auth. Verify with `dotnet --info` matching global.json.

children.title: CLI Usage
children.prompt: Practical guide to the `az` CLI. Show structured extension commands (e.g. `az group create ...`, `az vm ...`, `az config set/get/list`, `az login`, `az extension add/list`) using the help docs under `src/CLI/Help/Docs/` (config, deployment, disk, extension, group, login, logout, profile, rest, vm) as the authoritative command surface. Explain global flags classified in a single pass by `GlobalArgParser.Parse` (`src/CLI/Parser/GlobalArgParser.cs`) into a `GlobalArgs` record (`src/CLI/Parser/GlobalArgs.cs`): `--debug`, `--output json|plain`, `--no-cache` (sets AZCLIPS_NO_EXTENSION_CACHE at the call site), `--help` family, `--version` family. Note that unknown `--output` values raise a usage error at parse time. Explain shell completions (`src/CLI/Completions/CompletionGenerator.cs`, bash/zsh/ps1 scripts) and `--help` dispatch via `GlobalArgs.Help` / `RuntimeHelpDispatcher` (no more control-flow exceptions). Explain the `--profile`/global-profile override. Then explain the AI fallback UX: when a command fails and `agent.enabled` is true and the session is an interactive TTY, the CLI hands off to agent-mode (`TryAgentFallbackAsync`); note the non-interactive/CI guard and the AZCLIPS_IN_AGENT_MODE recursion guard. Include a Mermaid sequence diagram (autonumber) of parse -> execute -> fallback.

children.title: PowerShell Module Usage
children.prompt: Guide to the PowerShell surface. The cmdlet projects live under `src/PS/` (Cmdlets.Common, Cmdlets.Compute, Cmdlets.Config, Cmdlets.Login, Cmdlets.Resources — see `azclips.slnx`). Show importing modules and using cmdlets (e.g. `Connect-AzAccount`, `New-AzResourceGroup`, `New-AzVM`/`Get-AzVM` from `src/PS/Compute/Cmdlets/`, `Set-AzConfig` for config/telemetry opt-out per `README.md:160`). Explain how cmdlets share the SAME engine as the CLI: they call `AzclipsServiceProvider.Initialize(ClientType.PowerShell/...)` and resolve `IEngine`, then open an execution session whose output is pumped through a per-invocation channel back to `$PSCmdlet.WriteObject` — reference the thread-safety/output-routing notes in `src/Core/Core.Engine/Engine.cs:13-21` and `CmdletOutputStreamsFactory` (`src/PS/Common/CmdletOutputStreamsFactory.cs`). Note the .psd1 manifests and help markdown under each `src/PS/<Module>/help/`. Include a Mermaid diagram showing cmdlet -> Engine -> channel -> WriteObject.

modules.title: Deep Dive
modules.summary: Architecture-level explanations grouped by concern. Each leaf traces real code paths with file:line citations. Grouped into four themes so no section exceeds eight children.

children.title: Runtime Core
children.summary: The composition root, engine/session model, HTTP execution, and authentication that every command flows through.

children.title: Core Engine & Orchestration
children.prompt: The single most important architectural page. Trace the composition-root + session model and the CLI's try/execute/fallback orchestration. (1) DI bootstrap: `AzclipsServiceProvider` (`src/Core/Core.DependencyInjection/AzclipsServiceProvider.cs:17`) with `PrependRegistration`/`OverrideRegistration` (:29,:44), `RegisterAzclipsServices` chaining all module DIRegisterExtensions (:53), and idempotent `Initialize(ClientType)` (:67). Explain how each client (CLI `src/CLI/Program.cs:40-53`, TUI `TUI/Program.cs:23-41`) customizes registrations before Initialize. (2) The Engine: `Engine` is a partial mediator class (`src/Core/Core.Engine/Engine.cs:22`) implementing `IEngine` (`src/Core/Core.Abstractions/IEngine.cs:8`); it opens `ExecutionSession`/`DiscoverySession`, caches extension indices via `LFUCache<Lazy<IExtensionIndex>>` (:36,:81), and builds a per-invocation `ProcessorContext` in `CreateProcessorContext` (:99) including profile resolution (`ResolveProfileAsync` :143) and the HTTP pipeline with AuthHandler prepended. (3) ExecutionSession: channel-based isolated output, `RunAsync` -> `GetProcessor().ProcessAsync()` (`src/Core/Core.Engine/ExecutionSession.cs:57`), the global `--profile` pre-binding pass (per `openspec/changes/profile-management/design.md` Decision 4). (4) Orchestration/fallback: `Program.Main` try/catch (`src/CLI/Program.cs:65-145`) distinguishes structured `AzclipsErrorException` (no fallback) from `HttpRequestException`/generic exceptions that route to `TryAgentFallbackAsync` (:281). CRITICAL: explain that the historical 'OrchestratorEngine tries DefaultCommandEngine then falls back to AgentEngine' (per AGENTS.md / eng-docs/spec/ARCHITECTURE.md) is NOT the current code — the fallback is now an out-of-process TUI `--agent-mode` spawn; call this out as fact vs stale doc. Diagrams: component diagram of the DI graph + a sequence diagram (autonumber) of a full invocation with fallback.

children.title: HTTP Pipeline & Runtime
children.prompt: Explain the runtime HTTP execution layer in Core.Runtime. Cover `HttpPipeline` (`src/Core/Core.Runtime/HttpPipeline.cs`), `HttpPipelineService` (`HttpPipelineService.cs`), `HttpClientFactory`, and the delegating-handler composition: how `CreateProcessorContext` prepends the `AuthHandler.SendAsync` (`src/Core/Core.Engine/Engine.cs:115-135`), prepends a terminating step (`HttpPipelineTerminatingStep` — passthrough by default, terminates during client mocking) and appends a request-tracing step (`HttpRequestMessageTracingStep`) used for record/playback in tests. Explain retry policy (MaxRetries, MaxRetriesFor429, PollingInterval) sourced from `CoreOptions.Http`. Cover `SendAsyncFactory`/`SendAsyncTerminalFactory`, `RuntimeEventBus` (`src/Core/Core.Runtime/RuntimeEventBus.cs`) event publication, and `ConsoleOutputAdapter`/`ConsoleLoggingService`/`ScopedLoggingService` for output/log routing. Explain the `IProcessor`/`ProcessorContext` contract that extension commands implement. Diagram: the delegating-handler chain (auth -> terminating -> real send -> tracing) as a Mermaid flow.

children.title: Authentication (MSAL)
children.prompt: Explain the authentication subsystem. `MsalAuthService` (`src/Core/Core.Authentication/MsalAuthService.cs:11`) implements `IAuthService` (`src/Core/Core.Abstractions/IAuthService.cs`) using Microsoft.Identity.Client: ARM scope `https://management.core.windows.net//.default` (:12), public-client ClientId (:13), `LoginAsync` branching between device-code and interactive flows (:16), token cache persistence (`RegisterTokenCacheAsync`), and `AcquireTokenSilentlyAsync` used by the engine's AuthHandler. Explain `LogoutAsync(userPrincipalName)` (:29) — it removes only the account matching the active profile's UPN from the SHARED MSAL cache (per `openspec/changes/profile-management/design.md` Decision 6), not a blanket clear. Cover `AuthResultExtensions` and how `AuthResult` was extended to surface the account username. Explain the auth-context history: the old `AuthContext`/`context.json` was REMOVED and replaced by the resolved `Profile` flowing through `ProcessorContext.AuthHandler` (link to the Configuration & Profile Management page). Reference `eng-docs/spec/auth-context.md`. Diagram: sequence (autonumber) of `az login` -> MSAL interactive/device-code -> token cache -> profile save+activate.

children.title: Extensibility
children.summary: How commands are packaged, discovered, loaded, and configured — the extension model plus configuration and profiles.

children.title: Extension System
children.prompt: Explain the extension architecture end-to-end. (1) Anatomy of an extension: `IExtensionIndex` (`src/Core/Core.Abstractions/IExtensionIndex.cs`), an `ExtensionIndex.cs` command registry, `IProcessor` command implementations, and Customization/Processors (see `src/Extensions/Resources/` and `src/Extensions/Compute/`). (2) Discovery & loading: dispatch is uniform — every leaf comes from discovery over both loader tiers (`BundledExtensionLoader` and `InstalledExtensionLoader`) merged by `CliExtensionServiceRegistration.BuildLeafIndexWithDiscovery`, resolved by `ExtensionDispatcher` (`src/CLI/Parser/ExtensionDispatcher.cs:44`) and loaded by `CLIAssemblyLoadingProvider`/`ExtensionLoader` (`src/CLI/AssemblyLoading/`) and `IAssemblyLoadingService`; multi-version support via `InstalledExtensionLoader` (`src/CLI/Program.cs:58-59`). Extension index caching via LFUCache in Engine. (3) Extension management commands: add/list/pin/unpin/remove/show/update in `src/Extensions/Extension/` (`Add.cs`, `ExtensionInstaller.cs`, `DiscoveryBackedExtensionRegistry.cs`, `LocalArtifactProbe.cs`) with help under `src/CLI/Help/Docs/extension/`. (4) ExtensionRuntime: the serialization/type-conversion runtime (`src/Extensions/ExtensionRuntime/`) — JsonConverter framework, Conversions/Instances, Parser/Writers — that extensions use to (de)serialize ARM payloads. Reference `eng-docs/spec/extension-framework.md` and `eng-docs/spec/extension-management.md`. Diagram: extension resolution/loading sequence (autonumber).

children.title: Configuration & Profile Management
children.prompt: NEW feature area (#345). Two related but distinct concerns. (A) Configuration: the `Config` extension (`src/Extensions/Config/`) implements `az config get/set/list/delete/info` via processors (`Commands/GetConfigCommand.cs`, `SetConfigCommand.cs:9`, `ListConfigCommand.cs`, `DeleteConfigCommand.cs`, `InfoConfigCommand.cs`) sharing `ConfigCommandBase` (`Commands/ConfigCommandBase.cs:15`), which normalizes keys (dot/colon notation, `NormalizeKey` :39) and calls `IConfigurationService` (`src/Core/Core.Abstractions/IConfigurationService.cs`, impl in `src/Core/Core.Configuration/`). Config persists to `~/.azclips/config.json` (`src/Core/Core.Abstractions/HomePaths.cs:15`); known keys (e.g. `telemetry.enabled`, `agent.enabled`) come from typed options (`CoreOptions`, `AgentOptions`, `TelemetryOptions`); `--force` allows unknown keys. Mirror cmdlets in `src/PS/Config`. Reference `docs/azure-cli/docs-conceptual/config.md`, `eng-docs/spec/config-implementation.md`. (B) Profiles: `IProfileService`/`ProfileService` (`src/Core/Core.Runtime/ProfileService.cs:14`) store named connection profiles in `{LocalApplicationData}/.azclips/profiles.json` with a separate `active-profile` pointer, atomic temp+rename writes, and a `_gate` semaphore. Profile is the single source of truth for connection state and REPLACED the old AuthContext/context.json. Commands live in the Login extension: `ProfileListProcessor`, `ProfileShowProcessor`, `ProfileSetProcessor`, `ProfileRemoveProcessor` (`src/Extensions/Login/Processors/`). Explain login semantics (bare login -> reserved 'default' profile; `--out-profile <name>`; `--profile` re-auth; mutual exclusion) and the global `--profile` override resolved by `Engine.ResolveProfileAsync` (`src/Core/Core.Engine/Engine.cs:143`). Ground the design in `openspec/changes/profile-management/design.md` (Decisions 1-8) and its specs (profile-crud, profile-switching, login-profile-integration). Diagrams: profile state model + a sequence for `az login --out-profile prod` and `az group list --profile prod`.

children.title: AI & Interactive Experience
children.summary: The GitHub Copilot-powered agent and the interactive Terminal UI that hosts it.

children.title: AI Agent
children.prompt: Deep dive on the Agent/ project (Core.Agent.csproj). CRITICAL correction: the agent is built on the GitHub Copilot SDK (`GitHub.Copilot.SDK` 1.0.0, `Agent/Core.Agent.csproj:31`) driving a BUNDLED Copilot CLI daemon (`Agent/BundledDaemonResolver.cs:12`, resolves runtimes/<rid>/native/copilot). It is NOT Azure OpenAI/GPT-4o-mini — eng-docs/spec/ARCHITECTURE.md is stale; state this as fact vs stale doc. (1) `ChatAgent` (`Agent/ChatAgent.cs:23`): wraps `CopilotClient`/`CopilotSession`, exposes `SendAsync`, enforces the 'act-through-tools' contract with turn-closing tools (`_sendCalledClosingTool`, `LastSendCalledClosingTool` :34-49), 10-minute turn timeout, one-shot vs interactive session semantics (`SessionClosed`, `PlanShown`). (2) Tools (`Agent/Tools/`): `ProposePlanTool`, `SubmitResponseTool` (turn-closing), Help tools (`Tools/Help/HelpTools.cs` + HelpIndex.json/HelpManifest.json), Cache tools (`Tools/Cache/` — ARM resource cache: `ResourceCache`, `CachedResourceTools`, `ArmDetailsClient`, `AuthServiceTokenCredential`), Sku tools (`AvailableLocationsTool`). (3) Prompts (`Agent/prompts/inline.md`, `oneshot.md`, `tui.md`) selected by interaction mode. (4) Hosting/rendering (`Agent/Hosting/`): `ConsoleAgentRenderer`, `ConsoleApprovalPrompt` (y/n pump raced against SendAsync), `AbortKeyWatcher`, `SpinnerService`, `TraceAgentRenderer` (JSONL trace under agent.trace.path). (5) Environment probes (`Agent/Probes/`) and Hooks (`PlaceholderDetector`). Explain how agent-mode is entered from the CLI fallback (link to Core Engine page). Reference `eng-docs/spec/agent-experience.md`. Diagrams: agent turn lifecycle sequence (autonumber) + component diagram of ChatAgent/tools/renderers.

children.title: Terminal UI (TUI)
children.prompt: NEW top-level TUI project (Core.Tui.csproj) — must be its own page. Explain its two entry modes from `TUI/Program.cs:21`: (a) `--agent-mode` -> `AgentModeEntry.RunAsync` (`TUI/AgentMode/AgentModeEntry.cs`), the process spawned by the CLI on failure that owns the chat loop, banner, single-reader stdin, escape-valve turn limits (soft 12 / hard 20), prompt selection (inline vs oneshot), and optional JSONL trace; (b) the interactive full-screen shell built on the Hex1b terminal library (`TUI/Program.cs:23-60`). Cover the interactive shell: `AppState` (`TUI/AppState.cs`) + `AzureVfs` (`TUI/Azure/AzureVfs.cs`) presenting Azure resources as a virtual filesystem via `ArmClient` (`TUI/Azure/ArmClient.cs`); slash commands (`TUI/commands/`: Cd/Ls/Pwd/Copy/Exit/Mode/Refresh, `ISlashCommand.cs`); rendering (`TUI/Rendering/`: Header/Footer/History/MenuBar/Suggestion renderers, `TuiTheme`, `Ansi`); services (`TUI/services/`: CommandTree, CompletionService, HistoryService, ProcessService, PromptService, ClipboardService, AzclipsShellWorkload); TUI-specific DI overrides (`TuiLoggingService` silent logger, `TUITelemetryProvider` in `TUI/Program.cs:34-41`). Explain how it shares the same `AzclipsServiceProvider`/`IEngine` and how `AZCLIPS_IN_AGENT_MODE` prevents recursive agent spawns. Diagrams: TUI mode-selection flow + interactive shell component diagram.

children.title: Telemetry & Observability
children.prompt: Explain the telemetry subsystem (Core.Telemetry). `TelemetryService` (`src/Core/Core.Telemetry/TelemetryService.cs`) starts a root activity and per-command activities via System.Diagnostics ActivitySource (see `src/CLI/Program.cs:67,79` StartRootActivity/StartActivity and `TagInvocation`). Cover the privacy model: `DefaultTelemetryPropertyFilter`/`DefaultTelemetryActivityNameFilter` and their Processor variants strip parameter VALUES/URLs (only names + success/failure + env kept, per `README.md:153`), `TelemetryTags`/`TelemetryPropertyResolver`. Cover the async export path: `FileExporter` writes traces to disk, then a DETACHED background process re-invokes `az --upload-telemetry` (`src/CLI/Program.cs:34,410 SpawnTelemetryUploader`) which calls `TelemetryUpload.RunPending()` -> `TraceUploader` -> `TracerProviderExportSink` -> `WellKnownEndpoints` (Azure Monitor). Explain opt-out via `telemetry.enabled=false` (config), per-client `ITelemetryProvider` (CLITelemetryProvider/TUITelemetryProvider), and `TimingActivityListener`. Reference `eng-docs/spec/telemetry.md`. Diagram: activity capture -> file buffer -> detached uploader sequence (autonumber).

children.title: Testing & Benchmarking
children.prompt: Explain the test and benchmark strategy. Test projects (from `azclips.slnx`): `tests/Cli.Tests` (CLI integration: structured commands, agent fallback, typo correction), `tests/Cmdlets.Tests` (PowerShell cmdlets), `tests/Core.Extensions.Tests`, `tests/Core.Telemetry.Tests`, `tests/Common` (Tests.Common shared helpers), `tests/Fixtures/SharedAlpha`+`SharedBeta` (fixture extensions for assembly-loading/multi-version tests), `Agent/tests/Core.Agent.Tests` (agent tools, approval prompt, snapshot tests — e.g. `ClosingToolPredicateTests`, `ProposePlanValidationTests`, `EventRendererSnapshotTests`, `SnapshotTesting`), and `tools/Help/Azclips.Help.Tool.Tests`. Framework is xUnit with Coverlet coverage configured in `tests/Directory.Build.props` (per AGENTS.md). Explain the HTTP record/playback approach enabled by the pipeline tracing step (link to HTTP Pipeline page) and the terminating step used to mock clients. Explain `tests/Benchmark` (BenchmarkDotNet) and the `--no-cache`/in-process benchmark hooks: `GlobalArgParser` classifies `--no-cache` into `GlobalArgs.NoCache` and `Program.Main` sets `AZCLIPS_NO_EXTENSION_CACHE`; `SpawnTelemetryUploader` guards against benchmark host processes. Reference `eng-docs/spec/benchmark-workflows.md`. Cover test naming convention `MethodName_ShouldBehavior_WhenCondition` (AGENTS.md).
